s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of unilateral facial weakness and hemiplegia with impaired motor function
salient_findings: Incomplete closure of the right eye
Flattening of the right nasolabial fold
key_facts: 66-year-old man
24-hour history of symptoms
3-year history of hypertension
No history of neurological disorders
Alert and oriented
Effacement of the right frontal wrinkle
Incomplete closure of the right eyelid
Muscle strength in the right upper and lower extremities: grade 0/5
Hypoesthesia noted on the right side
Right Babinski sign: positive
Hemorrhage in the left thalamus-radiation crown region and in the lateral ventricle on CT scan
Corticobulbar tract appeared thinner on the left side than on the right on diffusion tensor imaging

shortlist.label: Intracerebral hemorrhage
shortlist.why_kept: Hemorrhage in the left thalamus-radiation crown region and in the lateral ventricle on CT scan

shortlist.label: Ischemic stroke
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of unilateral facial weakness and hemiplegia with impaired motor function

shortlist.label: Thalamic hemorrhage
shortlist.why_kept: Hemorrhage in the left thalamus-radiation crown region on CT scan

shortlist.label: Cerebral amyloid angiopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Hemorrhage in the lateral ventricle and thalamus, possible amyloid angiopathy-related hemorrhage

shortlist.label: Hypertensive encephalopathy
shortlist.why_kept: 3-year history of hypertension and acute onset of symptoms

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including incomplete closure of the right eye, flattening of the right nasolabial fold, and right-sided hemiplegia, are consistent with a thalamic hemorrhage, which is supported by the CT scan showing hemorrhage in the left thalamus-radiation crown region and in the lateral ventricle.

rejected.label: Intracerebral hemorrhage
rejected.why: While the patient does have an intracerebral hemorrhage, the specific location in the thalamus suggests a more specific diagnosis of thalamic hemorrhage.

rejected.label: Ischemic stroke
rejected.why: The presence of hemorrhage on the CT scan rules out ischemic stroke as the primary diagnosis.

rejected.label: Cerebral amyloid angiopathy
rejected.why: There is no evidence to suggest cerebral amyloid angiopathy, such as multiple lobar hemorrhages or a history of dementia.

rejected.label: Hypertensive encephalopathy
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings are more consistent with a localized lesion, such as a thalamic hemorrhage, rather than a diffuse process like hypertensive encephalopathy.

gold: Ipsilateral hemisphere hemorrhagic stroke with peripheral-type facial paralysis
